meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was the zero entered before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students draft in other places and paste it in, so what makes this more than a version history? Procedure first: was Owen asked about it before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote. Different editions, a line half remembered. Show me where he cites it, and I'll read the scene myself.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I'm reading the scene now. What exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and the final essay, that's what revision is. Is that your whole point on this one?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. A private rewrite, in writing tonight, before December 1, with nothing on his record. I'll take it to put this behind him. My points on the outline go in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Put Thursday, November 12 in the email with the time and the room. I'll confirm tonight. Anything else?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay after school on Thursday, November 12, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still want the time and room for that session confirmed, and my points on the outline comparison remain open. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants the time, room and written confirmation tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You turned your screen and gave the exact times from the version history, which she could check herself, and that is what first shifted her.
What cost ground: Nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence landed on a late night in October, the night before the essay was due, which is why she went shorter and harder, but it proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she pushed back that students change their argument between outline and essay, answer it right then with a sample of his other work instead of leaving that defence open.
